newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Deficit in Hungary budget to emerge in Feb-Fin Min.
newsitem.headline: Deficit in Hungary budget to emerge in Feb-Fin Min.

text.p: Hungary's January central state budget surplus will turn into a growing deficit in February and March, but this is not likely to push up government security yields, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.

"The monthly deficit is likely to rise to 70-80 billion forints ($460 million) in February and March (from a 15.7 billion forint surplus in January)," Finance Ministry Deputy Secretary of State Csaba Laszlo told a news conference on Thursday.
December tallied a budget deficit of 19.4 billion forints.
He said the January surplus was a seasonal phenomenon and had been repeated in previous years.
"In the past few years, the deficit always jumped in the second and the third months," Laszlo added.
He said the state treasury's account would be able to manage this fluctuation, and the government would not be compelled to increase the amount of its new security issues substantially.
"For that, the market will not feel a large increase in the state budget's financing needs because of the larger budget deficit," he said.
Laszlo added that January's 3.7-percent month-on-month rise in consumer prices, down from 4.4 percent in January 1996, was slightly better than the ministry expected.
The government's budget situation was as planned, with social security funds breaking-even in the first month, according to preliminary figures, Laszlo said.
Hungary's central state budget deficit target for 1997 is 359.7 billion forints.
-- Sandor Peto, Budapest newsroom + 36 1 327-4040 ($ = 173.9 Hungarian Forints)
